Scenario fixture: a11ycore-img-alt-present (“<img> must have an alt attribute”)

This file intentionally includes many edge cases to test eligibility and rule outcomes. Each test image has a stable id of the form img_case_XX. Images are tiny inline SVG data URLs to keep the fixture self-contained.

A. Baseline (eligible)

01 — FAIL: visible <img> missing alt
img Visible image, no alt attribute.
02 — PASS: visible <img> with non-empty alt
img Visible image with alt text.
03 — PASS (for this atomic rule): visible <img> with empty alt=""
img Empty alt is allowed here (decorative vs informative is handled by another rule/manual check).

B. Visible but excluded from AT (ineligible in acc target set)

04 — NEUTRAL/INELIGIBLE: visible aria-hidden="true" <img> missing alt
img Visible but aria-hidden. Missing alt.
Useful for comparing engines: some still flag missing alt even when aria-hidden.
05 — NEUTRAL/INELIGIBLE: visible aria-hidden="true" <img> with alt
img Visible but aria-hidden. Has alt.
06 — NEUTRAL/INELIGIBLE: <img> inside ancestor aria-hidden="true"
img Ancestor is aria-hidden; image missing alt.

C. Hidden by HTML/CSS (ineligible)

07 — NEUTRAL/INELIGIBLE: hidden attribute (missing alt)
img Hidden attribute; missing alt.
08 — NEUTRAL/INELIGIBLE: display:none (missing alt)
img display:none; missing alt.
09 — NEUTRAL/INELIGIBLE: visibility:hidden (missing alt)
img visibility:hidden; missing alt (space reserved).

D. Inertness (ineligible)

10 — NEUTRAL/INELIGIBLE: inert on <img> itself (missing alt)
img Image has inert attribute; missing alt.
Note: inert support varies; useful for engine comparison.
11 — NEUTRAL/INELIGIBLE: ancestor inert (missing alt)
img Ancestor is inert; image missing alt.

E. Exceptions that may remain eligible (focusable / IDREF-referenced)

12 — EXCEPTION CANDIDATE: aria-hidden="true" but focusable (tabindex="0"), missing alt
img Focusable image (tabindex=0) but aria-hidden; missing alt.
Per your engine exception, this may remain eligible for acc rules.
13 — EXCEPTION CANDIDATE: IDREF-referenced image, missing alt
ref
This element references the image id via aria-labelledby.
Referenced by IDREF; missing alt. (aria-hidden=true to force “exception” behavior if implemented.)
If your eligibility helper treats IDREF-referenced nodes as eligible, this should be evaluated.
14 — EXCEPTION CANDIDATE: aria-hidden="true" but focusable (tabindex="0"), alt present
img Focusable image (tabindex=0) but aria-hidden; alt present.
If your eligibility helper treats focusable nodes as eligible, this should be evaluated and pass (for this atomic rule).
15 — EXCEPTION CANDIDATE: hidden attribute but focusable (tabindex="0"), missing alt
img Hidden via HTML hidden but focusable; missing alt.
Tests the “hidden but focusable stays eligible” exception.
16 — EXCEPTION CANDIDATE: visibility:hidden but focusable (tabindex="0"), missing alt
img Hidden via CSS visibility, but focusable; missing alt.
Useful for comparing how engines treat focusability vs visibility-hidden.
17 — EXCEPTION CANDIDATE: inert but focusable (tabindex="0"), missing alt
img Image is inert but has tabindex; missing alt.
In browsers, inert usually prevents focus. Included to exercise your eligibility exception model and cross-engine behavior.
18 — FAIL (eligible): role="presentation" (also focusable), missing alt
img Presentational role; focusable; missing alt. Rule should ignore due to role exclusion.
This case verifies that the rule’s explicit role exclusion overrides other considerations.

F. Conditions that should NOT exclude eligibility (per engine guardrails)

19 — FAIL (eligible): opacity:0, missing alt
img Invisible via opacity, but should remain eligible; missing alt.
20 — FAIL (eligible): offscreen, missing alt
img Image is positioned far left (offscreen). It should remain eligible; missing alt.
21 — FAIL (eligible): zero-size box, missing alt
img Zero-size container; should remain eligible; missing alt.
22 — FAIL (eligible): role="presentation", missing alt
img Role presentation should not exclude eligibility; missing alt.
23 — FAIL (eligible): aria-disabled="true", missing alt
img aria-disabled should not exclude eligibility; missing alt.

G. Non-composed content (ineligible)

24 — NEUTRAL/INELIGIBLE: inside <template> (missing alt)
tpl Template contents are not composed into the DOM:

H. Aggregation / whole-rule behavior

25 — notApplicable candidate: only ineligible images
img Both images are ineligible (aria-hidden + hidden). If your rule requires at least one eligible image to pass, the outcome should be notApplicable.
26 — PASS candidate: eligible image passes; ineligible image missing alt should not fail
mix One eligible image has alt; the other is aria-hidden and missing alt.
27 — FAIL candidate: eligible image missing alt should fail even if other images are ineligible
mix Eligible image (left) is missing alt; other image is aria-hidden but has alt.

I. ARIA naming mechanism (aria-label / aria-labelledby satisfy without alt)

28 — PASS: <img> with aria-label, no alt
img ARIA naming (aria-label) is a valid text-alternative mechanism even without alt.
29 — PASS: <img> with aria-labelledby referencing non-empty text, no alt
img Dog photo label
30 — FAIL: <img> with aria-labelledby pointing to a non-existent id, no alt
img Dangling IDREF should not resolve to a name; alt is also missing.
31 — FAIL: <img> with aria-label="" (empty), no alt
img Empty aria-label does not satisfy ARIA naming; alt is also missing.

J. Visibility inheritance (invertible via explicit descendant override)

32 — FAIL (eligible): ancestor visibility:hidden, <img> itself explicitly visibility:visible, missing alt
img The image's own computed visibility is "visible" (explicit override), so it re-renders visible despite the hidden ancestor and remains eligible.
33 — NEUTRAL/INELIGIBLE: ancestor visibility:hidden, <img> inherits (no override), missing alt
img No explicit override; the image inherits visibility:hidden and stays ineligible.
34 — PASS: alt entirely absent, but a non-empty title attribute is present (found on a real site — AliExpress's homepage logo, 2026-07-23; a real HTML-AAM text-alternative fallback once alt is absent, also accepted by the reference engine's own image-alt rule)
img No alt attribute at all; title provides a real accessible name.

End of fixture.
